_doc: NALATI-MERGE A3: the Nalati score (MiniMax Music 3). gen_minimax.py --jobs nalati-jobs.json --keys test/dombra,... renders into <out>/<group>-<name>/minimax3-<seed>.wav. Step 1 = the six-take instrument test (can MiniMax play a dombra, a kobyz, a sybyzgy, a throat-sung drone convincingly?); the score's slots are added under `nalati/*` after the verdict. One Kazakh-folk score whatever the music-style setting (the user, wave 5); the throat drone only in the night + boss cues (wave 6).

test/dombra.prompt: Genre: Kazakh traditional folk, solo dombra kui. BPM: 120. Instrumental only, no vocals. A solo dombra - the two-string fretted Kazakh long-neck lute - played with fast strummed and plucked right-hand patterns, a galloping 6/8 horse-gait rhythm, open fifths on the drone string, the melody on the high string. Natural close recording in a felt yurt, no other instruments.

test/kobyz.prompt: Genre: Kazakh traditional folk, solo qobyz. BPM: 70. Instrumental only, no vocals. A solo kyl-kobyz - the ancient two-string horsehair bowed fiddle of the Kazakh shamans - a raw, breathy, rasping bowed tone full of overtones, slow sliding melody over its own low drone, haunting and wild, like wind over the steppe. Natural close recording, no other instruments.

test/sybyzgy.prompt: Genre: Kazakh traditional folk, solo sybyzgy. BPM: 80. Instrumental only, no vocals. A solo sybyzgy - the Kazakh open end-blown reed flute - an airy, breathy, wooden tone with a hummed throat drone under the melody, long free phrases with ornaments and slides, evoking a shepherd on a wide mountain pasture. Natural recording outdoors, no other instruments.

test/throat.prompt: Genre: Central Asian throat singing, overtone drone. BPM: 60. A single male throat singer (khoomei / kargyraa style) holding a deep growling drone with a whistling overtone melody above it, wordless, slow breaths between phrases, over a very soft low kobyz drone. Dark, ancient, night on the steppe. No drums, no other instruments.

test/ensemble-day.prompt: Genre: video game soundtrack, Kazakh folk ensemble. BPM: 112. Instrumental only, no vocals, no choir. An open-world adventure on the green Kazakh steppe of the Nalati grasslands. Arrangement: a strummed dombra ostinato in a galloping 6/8 horse-gait rhythm, a sybyzgy flute melody over it, a kobyz drone underneath, a jaw harp (shankobyz) twang and a frame drum (dauylpaz) keeping the gait. Wonder first, adventure second. No western orchestra, no piano, no guitar.

test/ensemble-night.prompt: Genre: video game soundtrack, Kazakh folk night theme. BPM: 66. The steppe at night under the stars in an open-world adventure game. Arrangement: a low wordless throat-sung drone (kargyraa) held under everything, a slow bowed kobyz melody, sparse plucked dombra notes, a soft frame drum like a distant heartbeat. Dark, calm, ancient, a little dangerous. No western orchestra, no piano, no guitar.
